profiles.summary: The public endpoint is served by two op-reth backends, one tagged v2.8.1-72207294 and one that reports no version. Both gave the specified word for all 185,529 battery and targeted vectors, and the deployed PoolManager bytecode gave the same bytes as on Ethereum for all 250 scripts.

deltas.delta: Six single web3_clientVersion requests to https://mainnet.optimism.io on 2026-11-24 returned op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 once and op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown five times, all behind one load balancer cookie and proxyd (x-proxyd-cache-status MISS). In 310 batches of three requests, 198 first entries named the dev build and 112 named v2.8.1. Commit 72207294 is the optimism revision that World Chain v2.8.2 pins for op-revm and alloy-op-evm.

The lockfile at tag op-reth/v2.9.0 equals the one at op-reth/v2.9.0-rc.1 byte for byte. Both pin revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, revm-bytecode 43.0.0, op-revm 20.0.0 and ruint 1.20.0. op-reth v2.8.1 pins revm 43.0.2 and revm-interpreter 43.0.1 with the same ruint 1.20.0.

revm-interpreter 43.0.1 and 43.0.2 are dependency bumps. The only interpreter fix since 42.0.0 that is not gated on Amsterdam is pull request 3864, which makes a failed memory resize halt with MemoryOOG. It concerns custom memory types that cannot grow; the shared memory of a node grows or runs out of gas first, so no result the PoolManager sees changes.

Rerun of the opdiff scripts on 2026-11-24: battery 99,985 of 99,985 and targeted 85,544 of 85,544 vectors match, pmdiff 250 of 250 scripts identical to Ethereum, 3,285 mined Swap events all satisfy the tick relation and 1,903 of 1,906 paired swaps match a single step to the unit, the other 3 being multi step.

profiles.summary: The v1.5.6 node already carries the EIP-8130 phased call executor, gated on the Everest upgrade, which has no date. Each phase runs under a journal checkpoint that also reverts transient storage, and transient storage is cleared only at commit_tx.

deltas.delta: eip8130.rs lines 1222 to 1344: phases dispatch calls from the sender, a reverting phase calls checkpoint_revert (line 1324) and later phases are skipped, a successful phase calls checkpoint_commit (line 1344), and commit_tx runs once per transaction (line 369). In revm main, checkpoint_revert reverts journal entries against transient storage (crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs lines 622 to 640) and commit_tx clears it (lines 141 to 158). The tag that matches revm 42.0.1 could not be read, so the revm half rests on the main branch.
everest.rs states that the Everest upgrade enables EIP-8130.

The BaseTime predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000030 is linked to its implementation since Denim (5 November 2026). Called from the PoolManager address it reverts on empty calldata, with or without value, and its setter rejects any caller but the depositor.

deltas.delta: EIP-1967 implementation slot of 0x4200...0030 holds 0xc0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d3c0d30030. The implementation (878 bytes) has the selectors 0x54fd4d50 (version), 0x86bdf394 (setTimestampMillisPart) and two getters.

eth_call from 0x498581ff718922c3f8e6a244956af099b2652b2b to 0x4200...0030: empty calldata with value 0 and with value 1 both revert; setTimestampMillisPart(10) reverts with 0x3c7b5203 at value 0 and with empty data at value 1.
The Denim specification puts a BaseTime deposit at transaction index 1 of every block, from 0xDeaDDEaDDeAdDeAdDEAdDEaddeAddEAdDEAd0001 with mint 0 and value 0, writing only slot 0 of the predeploy.

cleared.check: Assumption A1 on World Chain: does transient storage end at the transaction boundary (critic gap of cycle 5).
cleared.result: TLOAD in the second simulated transaction returned 0 after TSTORE in the first on two endpoints, with a positive control of 1 inside one call. Lock.sol:13-25 and CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 therefore see a fresh state per transaction in the simulation path.

cleared.check: EIP-8130 phased calls in the v1.5.6 node: can a phase leave the unlock flag or deltas of src/libraries/Lock.sol and CurrencyDelta.sol to a later phase or another sender.
cleared.result: All calls of one EIP-8130 transaction come from its own sender, so a later phase can only act on that sender's state, as in a multicall. unlock sets and clears the flag inside one call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), a reverting phase is rolled back with its transient writes, and commit_tx clears transient storage. The path is not active before Everest.

cleared.check: BaseTime predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000030 as the target of a native take (P1) or token take (P2) from the PoolManager.
cleared.result: A call from the PoolManager address with empty calldata reverts with and without value, so a native take reverts as a whole; the setter reverts for any caller but the depositor. A token take naming the predeploy as currency calls transfer, which is not one of its selectors, so it reverts.

cleared.check: Interop predeploys 0x4200...0022 to 0x30 on the six OP chains on 2026-11-24.
cleared.result: Only 0x2c and 0x2d have an implementation, as in cycle 7, so no new predeploy answers a call from the PoolManager.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses since cycle 7: the reth trie fault of November 2026, op-node v1.19.3 and v1.19.6 notes, the revm changelog, and the Hemi postmortem of a precompile panic reached through a force included deposit.
cleared.result: The trie fault is already cleared. The op-node notes concern gas limit derivation and decoding hardening. The Hemi case needs a panicking precompile; no such precompile is known on these chains, and the Base precompile size fault from the Beryl review is fixed in v1.5.6. None gives an ordinary account a path to PoolManager funds.

cleared.check: pmdiff5.py with the bytecode built from this checkout (PM_BUILD) on the seven chains: pools at extreme prices with liquidity up to 2^126, the 512 bit branch of mulDiv that decides the step outcome in SwapMath.sol:64-79.
cleared.result: All 137 scripts that the reference interpreter can run (5,074 calls, 513 failing with three revert selectors) give the reference answer on all seven chains, with the bytecode built from this checkout. A wrong MULMOD in the 512 bit branch would flip the comparison of amountRemainingLessFee with amountIn at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:69 and so the step outcome; it does not.

leads.question: When Everest activates on Base, rerun the transient storage and unlock checks inside an EIP-8130 transaction with several phases, and read the tagged revm journal for the version Base then pins.
leads.why: Phased calls are a new transaction boundary inside one transaction. The reading says they behave like a multicall of one sender, but the revm half rests on the main branch.

leadResults.answer: The endpoint has two op-reth backends behind proxyd: v2.8.1-72207294 and one built without version data (v0.0.0-dev-unknown), which answered most requests on 2026-11-24. Its commit, and so its revm and ruint versions, could not be identified from outside. With each of 310 chunks sent in a batch between two web3_clientVersion requests, all 185,529 battery and targeted vectors matched; 73,329 of them sat between two dev build tags and 19,200 between two v2.8.1 tags. proxyd can split a batch across backends, so the tags are strong but not conclusive. The OP Mainnet row of OPCODES.md holds for both backends; the identity of the dev build stays open as a low priority lead.
